reasoning: The test image shows a soybean leaf with interveinal chlorosis (yellowing between veins) and necrotic brown/purple spots concentrated toward the tip, with the green veins remaining somewhat intact. This pattern of interveinal yellowing with necrotic lesions is characteristic of Sudden Death Syndrome (SDS), which causes interveinal chlorosis and necrosis while leaf veins stay green longer. The pattern differs from Septoria brown spot (which shows more uniform small brown spots), Bacterial Pustule (which shows pustules), and Cercospora (different lesion pattern). The yellowing with dark necrotic areas bounded by veins is most consistent with SDS.
